title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 16.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 16, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Baasha king of Israel built Ramah
Asa brought out silver and gold
questions.correctAnswer: Baasha king of Israel built Ramah
questions.explanation: This event occurs in 2 Chronicles 16:1, making it the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who came up against Judah in the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign?
questions.explanation: Baasha king of Israel is mentioned as coming up against Judah in 2 Chronicles 16:1.

questions.question: What city did Baasha build to prevent movement in Judah?
questions.explanation: Ramah is the city that Baasha built as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:1.

questions.question: What did Asa bring out of the treasures to send to Benhadad?
questions.explanation: Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasures as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:2.

questions.question: Who was the king of Syria that Asa communicated with?
questions.explanation: Asa sent to Benhadad king of Syria, as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:2.

questions.question: What did Asa ask Benhadad to do regarding Baasha?
questions.explanation: Asa asked Benhadad to break his league with Baasha according to 2 Chronicles 16:3.

questions.question: What cities did Benhadad's captains smite?
questions.explanation: The captains smote Ijon and Dan as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:4.

questions.question: What action did Baasha take when he heard about Benhadad's attack?
questions.explanation: Baasha ceased his work on Ramah when he heard about the attack as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:5.

questions.question: What was Asa's relationship with Benhadad described as?
questions.explanation: Asa stated there was a league between him and Benhadad as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 16:3.

questions.question: Did Asa send gold and silver to Benhadad?
questions.explanation: Asa did send silver and gold to Benhadad as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:2.

questions.question: Where did Benhadad reside?
questions.explanation: Benhadad dwelt at Damascus as noted in 2 Chronicles 16:2.

questions.question: Did Benhadad listen to Asa's request?
questions.explanation: Benhadad hearkened unto king Asa, indicating that he listened to his request, as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:4.

questions.question: Did Asa's father have a league with Benhadad?
questions.explanation: Asa mentions a league between him and Benhadad, as there was between his father and Benhadad's father, as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:3.

questions.question: Did Asa request Baasha to attack Israel?
questions.explanation: Asa did not request Baasha to attack Israel; instead, he asked Benhadad to break his league with Baasha, as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:3.

questions.question: Did Baasha complete the building of Ramah?
questions.explanation: Baasha ceased building Ramah when he heard about Benhadad's attack, as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:5.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Asa do with the stones and timber of Ramah that Baasha was using for building?
options: He carried them away and used them to build Geba and Mizpah
He gave them to the king of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: He carried them away and used them to build Geba and Mizpah
questions.explanation: Asa took all Judah and carried away the stones of Ramah and the timber thereof, which Baasha was using to build, and built Geba and Mizpah with them, as stated in 2 Chronicles 16:6.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 16:8 promise will happen if someone relies on the LORD as Asa did in verse 7?
options: They will be delivered into their hand
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into their hand
questions.explanation: Verse 8 explains that because Asa relied on the LORD, even though the Ethiopians and Lubims were a huge host, God delivered them into his hand.

questions.question: Why did Hanani the seer come to Asa and rebuke him?
options: Because Asa relied on the king of Syria and not on the LORD
Because Asa built Geba and Mizpah
questions.correctAnswer: Because Asa relied on the king of Syria and not on the LORD
questions.explanation: Hanani told Asa that because he relied on the king of Syria instead of the LORD, the enemy escaped from his hand, as found in 2 Chronicles 16:7.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 16:9 explain the LORD's attitude towards those whose hearts are perfect toward Him in relation to Asa's actions in verse 7?
options: The LORD shows Himself strong in behalf of them
The LORD causes wars for the perfect-hearted
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shows Himself strong in behalf of them
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states that the eyes of the LORD run to and fro to show Himself strong in behalf of those with perfect hearts, implying Asa erred by not relying on God as he should have in verse 7.

questions.question: What consequence did Asa face for his reliance on the king of Syria instead of God?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 warns Asa that because he acted foolishly by not relying on God, he would have wars from that time forward.

questions.question: What was Asa's reaction to Hanani's rebuke?
questions.explanation: Asa was angry with Hanani and put him in a prison house because of the rebuke, as described in 2 Chronicles 16:10.

questions.question: What additional wrong did Asa commit at the same time he imprisoned Hanani?
options: He oppressed some of the people
questions.correctAnswer: He oppressed some of the people
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time he put Hanani in prison.

questions.question: How did Asa respond to Baasha building Ramah according to the earlier verses?
options: He sent silver and gold to Benhadad to break his alliance with Baasha
questions.correctAnswer: He sent silver and gold to Benhadad to break his alliance with Baasha
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:2-3 shows Asa sent silver and gold to Benhadad king of Syria to break his league with Baasha.

questions.question: What was the effect of Asa's alliance with Benhadad on Baasha's plans?
options: Baasha formed an alliance with Asa
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states that when Baasha heard of the alliance, he stopped building Ramah.

questions.question: What does Asa’s example teach about relying on human alliances instead of God?
options: It can result in failure and future conflict
It is the wisest course of action
questions.correctAnswer: It can result in failure and future conflict
questions.explanation: Asa relied on the king of Syria instead of God, resulting in the enemy escaping and wars from then on, as per verses 7 and 9.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith can Christians learn from Asa’s reaction to the seer Hanani?
options: Rebuke should be welcomed as correction
Anger is the best response to criticism
Prison is the right punishment for prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Rebuke should be welcomed as correction
questions.explanation: Asa’s anger and imprisonment of Hanani contrast with the biblical principle of accepting godly rebuke, shown in 2 Chronicles 16:10.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 16:9 emphasize the importance of a perfect heart toward God?
options: God ignores those with perfect hearts
God shows His strength on behalf of those with perfect hearts
questions.correctAnswer: God shows His strength on behalf of those with perfect hearts
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states that the eyes of the LORD run to and fro to show Himself strong for those with perfect hearts.

questions.question: What does Asa’s use of Baasha’s building materials to fortify Geba and Mizpah illustrate?
options: Using enemy resources wisely is strategic
questions.correctAnswer: Using enemy resources wisely is strategic
questions.explanation: Asa repurposed Baasha's materials to strengthen his own defenses, showing strategic wisdom in 2 Chronicles 16:6.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 16:9, God actively looks throughout the earth to support those whose hearts are perfect toward Him.
questions.explanation: Verse 9 clearly states that the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth to show Himself strong on behalf of those with perfect hearts.

questions.question: True or False: Asa's putting Hanani in prison was an example of godly humility and repentance.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:10 shows Asa was angry and imprisoned Hanani, which does not reflect godly humility or repentance.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 16.

questions.question: What did Asa do in response to Baasha's threat against Judah?
options: He sought help from the LORD
He sent silver and gold to Benhadad
questions.correctAnswer: He sent silver and gold to Benhadad
questions.explanation: Asa sent silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the king's house to Benhadad king of Syria as a response to Baasha's threat (2 Chronicles 16:2).

questions.question: How did Asa react to the message from Hanani the seer?
options: He sought guidance from the LORD
He called for a national prayer
questions.explanation: Asa was wroth with Hanani the seer and put him in a prison house because he was angry at the message he received (2 Chronicles 16:10).

questions.question: In which year of his reign did Asa become diseased in his feet?
questions.explanation: Asa became diseased in his feet in the thirty and ninth year of his reign (2 Chronicles 16:12).

questions.question: What did Asa seek for his disease instead of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Asa sought not to the LORD, but to the physicians for his disease (2 Chronicles 16:12).

questions.question: Where was Asa buried after his death?
options: In the valley of the kings
In the temple of the LORD
questions.explanation: Asa was buried in his own sepulchres in the city of David (2 Chronicles 16:14).

questions.question: What did the people prepare for Asa's burial?
options: Sweet odours and divers kinds of spices
questions.correctAnswer: Sweet odours and divers kinds of spices
questions.explanation: They laid Asa in the bed filled with sweet odours and divers kinds of spices prepared by the apothecaries' art (2 Chronicles 16:14).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'disease' in 2 Chronicles 16:12 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'disease' in this context refers to an affliction or illness that Asa suffered.

questions.question: Which literary device is used when Asa is described as not seeking the LORD?
questions.explanation: It is ironic that a king who previously relied on the LORD in battle chose not to seek Him in his time of personal affliction.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Asa's reliance on physicians instead of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Matthew 9:12 relates to the theme of seeking healing and emphasizes that Jesus came to call sinners, not the righteous, indicating the importance of seeking divine help.

questions.question: Which other passage reflects on the consequences of Asa's actions in relying on man rather than the LORD?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 17:5 discusses the curse on those who trust in man, resonating with Asa's failure to rely on the LORD (2 Chronicles 16:7-9).

questions.question: What comes immediately before Asa's imprisonment of Hanani the seer?
questions.explanation: Hanani the seer delivers a message to Asa, and immediately following this, Asa reacts by imprisoning him (2 Chronicles 16:10).

questions.question: What comes immediately after Asa's death?
options: He was succeeded by his brother
questions.explanation: After Asa died, his son Jehoshaphat succeeded him as king of Judah (2 Chronicles 16:13).

questions.question: The word 'king' in 2 Chronicles 16:2 refers to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The 'king' mentioned in 2 Chronicles 16:2 refers to Baasha, the king of Israel, who was the adversary of Asa at that time.

questions.question: Asa's reliance on Benhadad instead of the LORD demonstrates what biblical principle?
questions.explanation: Asa's reliance on Benhadad rather than the LORD illustrates the biblical principle of trusting in God rather than man (2 Chronicles 16:7-9).

questions.question: Asa's actions were entirely righteous throughout his reign.
questions.explanation: Asa's actions, particularly not seeking the LORD in his disease, demonstrate that he was not entirely righteous, leading to consequences (2 Chronicles 16:12).

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 16:7 teach about human sin and reliance?
options: Human reliance on political alliances rather than God is sinful and leads to failure.
Human wisdom in diplomacy is the surest path to peace.
Reliance on God is secondary to military strength.
Human sin is excused when motivated by fear.
questions.correctAnswer: Human reliance on political alliances rather than God is sinful and leads to failure.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:7 explicitly states that Asa's reliance on the king of Syria rather than the LORD caused the failure and escape of the enemy, indicating that misplaced reliance is sinful.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 16:9 teach about God's nature in relation to the hearts of people?
options: God actively searches the earth to support those with perfect hearts toward Him.
God is indifferent to the moral state of individuals.
God only intervenes sporadically based on human efforts.
God's strength is revealed only through natural events.
questions.correctAnswer: God actively searches the earth to support those with perfect hearts toward Him.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:9 states that the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the earth to show Himself strong for those whose hearts are perfect toward Him, teaching God's active involvement in human affairs.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is implied by Asa's failure in 2 Chronicles 16:12?
options: True sanctification involves seeking the LORD even in physical affliction rather than relying solely on human means.
Sanctification is unnecessary when one has ruled righteously.
Physical healing is guaranteed regardless of spiritual condition.
Seeking physicians is sufficient for spiritual and physical health.
questions.correctAnswer: True sanctification involves seeking the LORD even in physical affliction rather than relying solely on human means.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:12 shows Asa's failure to seek the LORD in his disease and his reliance on physicians, implying a lack of sanctification in trusting God fully.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 16:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:9 describes the LORD's eyes running to and fro throughout the earth, demonstrating His omniscience in knowing all hearts and actions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 2 Chronicles 16:8 by God delivering Judah despite their enemies' numerical superiority?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:8 speaks of God delivering Judah despite a huge enemy host, showing God's sovereign power over human strength and numbers.

questions.question: How does the narrative of 2 Chronicles 16 prepare for New Testament themes of faith and reliance on God?
options: It illustrates the consequences of misplaced trust, anticipating teachings on faith in Christ alone.
It focuses only on political alliances, unrelated to New Testament faith.
It endorses pragmatic alliances over divine reliance.
It denies the need for faith in God's promises.
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the consequences of misplaced trust, anticipating teachings on faith in Christ alone.
questions.explanation: The chapter shows Asa's failure when trusting a foreign king instead of God, highlighting a theological principle echoed in the New Testament about faith and reliance solely on Christ (cf. Romans 4:3).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Chronicles 16:13 make by noting Asa's death after spiritual failure?
options: It underscores human mortality and the need for eternal life through Christ.
It emphasizes the success of human kingship.
It teaches that death is always a reward for sin.
It connects Asa's death to the destruction of the temple.
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores human mortality and the need for eternal life through Christ.
questions.explanation: Asa's death after failing to seek God highlights the reality of mortality and points forward to the New Testament promise of eternal life through Christ (Hebrews 9:27).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 16:7 and 16:9 teach about the relationship between human faith and divine support?
options: Human faith in God is necessary to receive His active support and deliverance.
Divine support is automatic regardless of human faith.
Faith and divine support are unrelated concepts.
Human political strategy is superior to divine intervention.
questions.correctAnswer: Human faith in God is necessary to receive His active support and deliverance.
questions.explanation: Verse 7 condemns reliance on human alliances instead of God, while verse 9 highlights God's active support for those with perfect hearts, teaching that faith is essential for divine help.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 16:12 and 16:10 teach about the consequences of rejecting prophetic rebuke and divine dependence?
options: Rejecting God's prophet results in spiritual and physical decline.
Prophetic rebuke has no real consequence.
Physical illness absolves one from spiritual responsibility.
Divine dependence is optional for rulers.
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting God's prophet results in spiritual and physical decline.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 shows Asa's anger and imprisonment of Hanani, the seer, and verse 12 describes Asa's severe disease and failure to seek God, together illustrating the negative consequences of rejecting God's word.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 16:4 and 16:6 teach about God's providence in human history?
options: God uses foreign nations to accomplish His purposes and provides for restoration through human agency.
God is passive in wars and human affairs.
Human actions alone determine historical outcomes.
questions.correctAnswer: God uses foreign nations to accomplish His purposes and provides for restoration through human agency.
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows God using Benhadad's army against Israel, and verse 6 depicts Asa using the stones from Ramah to build other cities, reflecting divine providence over history and restoration.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Asa's reliance on the king of Syria shows that God is unreliable. What does 2 Chronicles 16:7-9 actually teach?
options: God is reliable, but human disobedience in seeking alliances instead of Him leads to failure.
God is unreliable and requires human alliances.
God punishes all kings regardless of faith.
God is indifferent to human choices.
questions.correctAnswer: God is reliable, but human disobedience in seeking alliances instead of Him leads to failure.
questions.explanation: Verses 7-9 show Asa's failure due to misplaced trust and God's active support for those who rely on Him, teaching God's reliability contingent on human faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 16:14 teach about the cultural practice of honoring the dead and its theological implications?
options: Honoring the dead with burial and spices reflects the belief in bodily resurrection and sanctity of the body.
Funerary customs have no theological significance.
The use of spices denies resurrection hope.
questions.correctAnswer: Honoring the dead with burial and spices reflects the belief in bodily resurrection and sanctity of the body.
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes burial with spices and a sepulchre, reflecting an ancient practice that honors the body, consistent with biblical teaching on resurrection (cf. Job 19:26).

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 16:9 reveal by highlighting God's support for the perfecthearted?
questions.explanation: God's eyes running throughout the earth in verse 9 illustrate His omnipresence, being present everywhere to support the perfecthearted.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 16:1-6 illustrate the theological principle of God's permissive will in human political affairs?
options: God allows human political actions, such as Baasha building Ramah, but uses them to fulfill His sovereign purposes.
God directly commands all political decisions without human involvement.
Human political affairs occur independently of God's will.
Political actions are always contrary to God's plan.
questions.correctAnswer: God allows human political actions, such as Baasha building Ramah, but uses them to fulfill His sovereign purposes.
questions.explanation: Verses 1-6 show human political maneuvers and their outcomes, yet God providentially orchestrates these events to accomplish His purposes through Asa's response and Benhadad's intervention.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 16:8 and 16:9 teach about divine deliverance and human faith?
options: Divine deliverance is granted to those who place their trust in God rather than in military might.
Deliverance depends solely on human military strength.
Faith is unnecessary for experiencing God's power.
God delivers based on nationality, not faith.
questions.correctAnswer: Divine deliverance is granted to those who place their trust in God rather than in military might.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 recounts victory despite enemy strength due to reliance on God, and verse 9 stresses God’s active support for faithful hearts, combining to teach the necessity of faith for deliverance.
